lacuna.current_status: Read 2026-09-15. (1) The canonical published step decomposition is Pope et al., "Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference" (arXiv:2211.05102, Nov 2022; MLSys 2023): decode at small batch is weight-streaming bound, t_step ~ weight_bytes / memory_bandwidth, with a compute-intensity threshold separating the bandwidth-bound and math-bound regimes as batch grows. (2) The framing instrument is the roofline model (Williams, Waterman, Patterson, CACM 52(10):65-76, Oct 2009): arithmetic intensity vs the machine knee (peak FLOP/s over peak B/s); the survey "LLM Inference Unveiled: Survey and Roofline Model Insights" (arXiv:2402.16363, Feb 2024) applies exactly this to per-stage LLM inference and states the batch-1 decode memory-bound result. Kipply's "Transformer Inference Arithmetic" (kipp.ly, Aug 2023) popularized the same per-step byte accounting (weights + KV + activations) for decode. (3) Attention at small batch has its own regime map: Flash-Decoding (PyTorch blog, Oct 2023; Stanford CRFM post 2023-10-12) names the parallelism starvation - decode attention at batch 1-8 cannot saturate DRAM from the batch axis alone and splits the KV sequence across SMs to restore occupancy ("load the KV cache in parallel as fast as possible, then combine"); FlashInfer (arXiv:2501.01005, Jan 2025; MLSys 2025) productizes the schedule choice, auto-selecting split-KV vs non-split per batch/ctx via its plan() API (docs: "Scheduling, tile selection, and split-KV reduction are automatic implementation details"). PagedAttention (Kwon et al., SOSP 2023) is the paged-KV access model both assume. (4) The regime-classification measurement workflow is standard Nsight: Nsight Compute Speed-Of-Light section (SM% vs Memory% of theoretical; both low = latency-bound, per NVIDIA's SOL explainer, forums.developer.nvidia.com 2022) then Memory Workload Analysis (achieved DRAM %), Launch Statistics and Occupancy (grid vs SM count, register/smem limiters); the standard four-section base set is documented in NASA HECC's NCU guide (nsas.nasa.gov, current) - plus Nsight Systems for the step timeline and inter-kernel gaps. This host has already run the workflow once profitably: MEMORY.md 2026-09-13 - the ncu profile named the wall as "L1/smem 84.5 pct, 11.2 of 32 lanes active, 30.3 pct barrier stalls, occupancy smem-limited at 2 CTAs/SM, DRAM 3 pct", which directed the +20% register-accumulator surgery. (5) Turing-level constants for the model exist in microbenchmark form: Jia, Tillman, Maggioni, Scarpazza, "Dissecting the NVidia Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking" (arXiv:1903.07486, Mar 2019) gives Turing cache/TLB latencies (L1 32 cycles, shared 23, L2 236 cycles on T4) and the pointer-chase methodology for DRAM latency (several-hundred-ns class [uncertain: exact TU102 DRAM load-to-use latency is unmeasured on this host]). (6) calx-mill is org prior art, not in this repo (CONSOLIDATION.md T9: "calx-mill (the performance-model instrument; its TU102 adapter's next lane is exactly plan/0002#performance-model)"); no public source documents its internals, so the adapter structure below is the generic pattern such instruments follow, to be mirrored against the org's actual code when accessible.
lacuna.applicability: The method transfers fully because every device constant it needs is already measured and banked here rather than spec'd: 535 GB/s LDG wall, ~101 TFLOP/s FP16-accumulate at the locked 1455 MHz, the 2-resident-CTA occupancy law, the conflicted-STS halves, 43.7 GB/s NVLink (plan/0004), and the M*=47 W4A16 crossover (itself a roofline output: "a model output and initial hypothesis, not a constant" per plan/0002). What is Turing-specific and binding: (a) no cp.async/TMA means latency-hiding relies on register/LDSM staging and enough CTAs, so the latency-vs-bandwidth split of the regime map is the load-bearing half - a kernel below the byte floor at a sub-wave grid cannot be fixed by tiling; (b) CUDA graphs are on, so per-node cost is a GPU-side gap (~1-2 us/node [uncertain: measure on this pair], not the ~5-10 us eager launch) and NCU kernel replay distorts graph concurrency - durations should come from the plan/0010 nsys ledger, counters from NCU on isolated kernels at engine shapes; (c) TU102 L2 is ~5.5 MiB [uncertain: per TU102 whitepaper class], comparable to a batch-4 ctx-slice of KV, so byte counts that ignore L2 residency overestimate some kernels. What does NOT transfer: published regime thresholds from Hopper/Ampere serving papers (their balance knees are 10-30x our 188.8 FLOP/B knee); any model constant taken from spec sheets (672 GB/s GDDR6 nominal overstates the measured wall by ~26%). The method's deliverable here is a verdict on the ~4.3 ms: it decides between byte-floor, bandwidth-regime (falsified territory per plan/0009), latency-regime, and step-structure buckets BEFORE kernel-lane days are spent - and it is the missing half of the open plan/0002#performance-model task.

design.mechanism: RECIPE - per-kernel latency-vs-bandwidth regime model of one decode step. Inputs: (i) per-launch work table (kernel name, bytes read+written incl. weights/KV/activations/workspace, FLOPs, grid geometry in CTAs and warps, calls per step); (ii) measured device constants. Constants for TU102 (all measured on this host, 2026-08-27 unless noted): BW_wall = 535 GB/s; peak fp16-acc = 101 TFLOP/s at 1455 MHz (int8 = 203 TOPS); machine knee = 101e12/535e9 = 188.8 FLOP/B; DRAM latency ~0.5-0.7 us [uncertain - one pointer-chase probe closes this, mirroring arXiv:1903.07486]; graph-replayed per-node gap ~1-2 us [uncertain - read from nsys]; AR latency fit a+b*s (see nccl-tp2-step-cost item). Step 1: classify each launch. AI_i = flops_i/bytes_i; memory-bound if AI_i < 188.8 FLOP/B (at batch 4 every GEMM and attention launch qualifies - see worked example). Within memory-bound, split regime: bandwidth-critical if the grid can cover the in-flight demand, CTAs_i * bytes_in_flight_per_CTA >= BW_wall * t_DRAM (~321 KB at 600 ns, Little's law); else latency-critical (duration is set by stall chains and wave count = CTAs_i/(68 SMs x 2 CTA law), not by bytes). Step 2: predict each launch t_i = max(bytes_i/BW_wall, flops_i/peak, latency_floor_i). Step 3: compose the step in dependency order: T_step = sum(t_i) + sum(gaps) + sum(AR), where gaps are the nsys-measured inter-node costs under graphs. Step 4: floor = weights/BW_wall + KV/BW_wall + activations/BW_wall + N_AR * t_AR + irreducible serialization. Step 5: attribute the residual (T_measured - T_floor) by kernel class, and validate bucket-by-bucket against the #step-profile ledger and NCU (SOL: both bars low = latency regime confirmed; Memory Workload Analysis: achieved DRAM % of 535; warp-state long_scoreboard = DRAM latency; barrier stalls = sync chain). Step 6: regress the adapter's constants predicted-vs-measured per device - exactly plan/0002#performance-model's lane. WORKED EXAMPLE at the host geometry (batch 4, ctx 2048, 32 layers = 24 GDN + 8 full-attn d256, hidden 2560, W4A16, TP2). Bytes: weights 9.47e9 B/rank (= 17.7e-3 s x 535e9 B/s; the record's '~9 GiB' rounds 8.82 GiB - exactly 9.0 GiB would give 18.06 ms, the record's 55.4 tok/s derivation). KV = 0.12e-3 x 535e9 = 64.2 MB = 7.65 KiB/token over 8192 tokens = ~980 B/token/layer across 8 d256 layers, consistent with ~1 KV head fp16 at d256 (2 x 1 x 256 x 2 B = 1024 B) [uncertain: kv-head count; anchor on the measured 0.12 ms]. Activations: 32 layers x 8 tensors x (4 x 2560 x 2 B) = 5.24 MB -> 9.8 us - negligible. GEMM regime: a 2560x2560 out_proj at M=4: AI = 2*4*2560*2560 / (2*(4*2560 + 2560*2560 + 4*2560)) = 3.99 FLOP/B, 47x below the 188.8 knee -> memory-bound; t = 13.15 MB / 535 GB/s = 24.6 us; summed over all Marlin GEMMs this IS the 17.7 ms weight stream (M*=47 says every decode GEMM sits in this byte regime). Attention regime: KV read is 0.12 ms at the wall; the walk grid at batch 4 exposes 4 seqs x PPS splits x heads CTAs against 136 CTA slots (68 SMs x 2) - sub-wave (the outline's 0.17-wave figure) - so in-flight bytes fall short of the ~321 KB Little's-law demand and the kernel is latency-critical unless splits lift the CTA count; the combine kernel adds a second launch plus a workspace write-then-read dependency (~0.66 MB round-trip at batch 4 x 10 heads x 256 x 2 B x2 = ~1.2 us at the wall - bytes negligible, latency structural). Collectives: 64 ARs x 20.48 KB (see nccl-tp2-step-cost): one-shot 3-7 us/call -> 0.19-0.45 ms. FLOOR: T_floor = 17.70 + 0.12 + 0.01 + 0.19..0.45 = 18.0-18.3 ms (with NCCL-class AR: 18.5-19.4 ms). ATTRIBUTION: measured TRITON arm 19.96 ms (50.1 tok/s) sits ~1.7-2.0 ms above floor - near floor, healthy. Measured champion 24.27 ms (41.2 tok/s) sits ~6.2 ms above floor; the 4.31 ms delta vs TRITON cannot be byte volume (KV is 0.12 ms; the workspace round-trip ~1.2 us) -> it is latency-regime + structure: 4.31 ms / 8 full-attn layers ~ 539 us/layer of excess duration [uncertain: the ledger owns the attn-vs-GDN-vs-gap split]. The model therefore predicts (i) NCU at engine shapes shows low DRAM% with high stall% on the owned walk/combine - the same signature as the banked 2026-09-13 profile (2 CTA/SM, 30.3% barrier stalls, DRAM 3% pre-surgery); (ii) surgery lives in grid exposure (split/head axis), workspace elimination (fuse combine into the walk), and launch/serialization structure - NOT in tile or bandwidth work, which plan/0009 falsified; (iii) the gap+AR structure terms sum to ~0.5-1 ms/step (150-170 launches/step per the gdn-step-coupling source read at 1-2 us/node + 0.3 ms AR), leaving ~3-5 ms in kernel durations - the ledger quantifies each. CALX-MILL ADAPTER MIRROR - how such adapters are typically structured, so the host can rebuild one from banked constants: (a) a device constants table, measured not spec'd (BW_wall, peak FLOPs at locked clock, knee, DRAM latency, cache latencies/sizes, launch/gap costs eager vs graph, per-collective latency fit a+b*s, occupancy law); (b) op cost functions behind one interface - GEMM(M,N,K): bytes=(MK+KN+MN)*elsize, flops=2MNK, t=max(bytes/BW, flops/peak) with the crossover M* derived not hardcoded; attention-decode(batch,ctx,heads,d,kv_heads,splits): bytes=KV+q/o+workspace, t=max(bytes/BW, parallelism floor), split heuristic from the CTA-count rule; collective(size,world): t=a+b*size/links_bw; memory-op(bytes)=bytes/BW; (c) a step composer that walks the launch table in dependency order and sums; (d) the predicted-vs-measured regression lane - run engine shapes, fit constants, report model error per op class (plan/0002: "Record model error per contended mix; the model is a filter, not the final arbiter"). The banked characterization JSONs on the fork branch (MEMORY.md 2026-08-27: raw at 5197c50) are the constants source.
design.failure_modes: (1) Spec-sheet bandwidth poisons the model: 672 GB/s nominal vs 535 GB/s measured wall is a 26% error on every prediction - use measured constants only (the host rule "TP2 communication is measured, not spec'd" generalizes to everything). (2) Byte-accounting errors: omitting workspace round-trips or activation traffic biases AI and hides the latency regime; conversely ignoring L2 (~5.5 MiB [uncertain]) overestimates bytes for small working sets that stay resident across the split/combine pair. (3) The classic roofline is blind to the latency regime - an AI-below-knee kernel at a sub-wave grid can sit 10x above its byte time with the roofline still calling it 'at the wall' if achieved BW is compared to achieved BW; the two-way split (bandwidth- vs latency-critical via Little's law + wave count) is the fix, and NCU's SOL section is the instrument. (4) Derived constants drift: M*=47 is "an initial hypothesis, never as a constant" (plan/0002); same for every knee and latency - regress per device and per clock lock. (5) NCU replay artifacts: kernel replay serializes graph nodes and flushes caches; durations from NCU can contradict nsys - take counters from NCU, time from the step ledger, and say which is which in the ledger (the 2026-09-13 session already needed the same-binary-PPS discipline). (6) Wave quantization: at 0.17-wave occupancy, predictions change discretely with split count (4->8 splits can double exposed CTAs); model the step at the exact engine grid, not as a smooth function. (7) The engine-context inversion precedent (MEMORY.md 2026-09-13/0009: a kernel 3x faster isolated made the step 3.6 ms slower) means isolated-kernel predictions must be gated through the in-engine A/B before they move committed rows - the model culls, the ledger decides.
design.effort_estimate: Doctrine + 1-2 CPU-side days: author the constants table and op functions from banked measurements (characterization JSONs, PROFILE-DELTA.md, ledger) into the calx-mill-mirroring adapter; two half-day GPU probes close the open constants (TU102 DRAM latency pointer-chase; graph-replayed per-node gap from the existing nsys captures). No kernel-lane work. Feeds the already-open plan/0002#performance-model task.
design.priority_signal: Moderate - the instrument, not a lever. It moves no milliseconds itself, but it is the cheapest cull instrument for the plan/0010 surgery shortlist: with bandwidth-level levers falsified (plan/0009) and the short-row engine-context inversion still open, the roofline decomposition is what decides whether the ~4.3 ms is latency-regime (grid-exposure surgeries pay), structure (fusion/launch-count surgeries pay), or already-floor (stop). The worked example says: floor 18.0-18.3 ms, TRITON arm ~2 ms above floor, the 4.3 ms residual is kernel-duration/structure, not bytes - so it directly licenses the structural surgeries and kills tile-level proposals before kernel-lane days are spent. It also closes a committed-plan gap: #performance-model is an open task with a named instrument and no landed model.
